old_caption: The video captures a dramatic scene inside a white washing machine, where a pile of white paper cups is engulfed in flames. The fire starts small but quickly intensifies, with bright orange and yellow flames licking at the edges of the cups. The cups are stacked in a circular pattern, creating a dense arrangement that allows the fire to spread rapidly. As the flames grow, they consume more of the paper, causing the cups to crumple and collapse under the heat. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, focusing on the central action within the machine. The background is minimal, with only the edge of the washing machine door visible, emphasizing the intensity of the fire. The video ends with the fire still burning fiercely, highlighting the destructive power of the flames against the simple, everyday object of the paper cups.

caption: The video captures a largely fixed close-up view into the open circular opening of a white front-loading appliance, its door swung to the left. The lower half of the drum is packed with empty white paper tubes in a honeycomb of circular cross-sections, while the upper half holds curled, partly charred paper pieces that are actively burning. Bright orange-yellow flames rise continuously from these pieces toward the top of the drum, their shape, height and brightest tongues flickering from frame to frame. The overall fire stays confined to the upper region, and the glowing edges of the charred paper remain in roughly the same positions. The lower paper tubes are not burning, intact and visually fixed in place throughout. A barcode sticker sits at the top edge, and two screws and a small black rectangular part are fixed on the right side of the opening. The appliance body and open door remain visually stationary, with little or no camera movement evident.

review_issues.problem: Describing the view as static overstates stillness; the flames change shape and brightness continuously, so the framing should be qualified as largely fixed.
The lower tubes are illuminated by the fire, though they are not burning; "unlit" can imply absence of light rather than absence of ignition.
This is an absolute claim of no motion; the visible frames support only little or no camera movement.
